A network of possibilities.
Connected through work.

A song can become part of a collection. A garden can supply an ingredient. A club can bring people together around a useful product.

A connection begins
with an exchange.

Name what is contributed, where it comes from, who is involved and the terms of use. A project retains its own purpose and can connect to several activities at once.

Explore, then agree.

These are reference connections from the plan. They do not establish partnerships, grant artwork rights or confirm anyone’s participation.

More ways in.

Garden Mate, Kitchen Mate, Fermentation Mate and Event Mate connect growing, preparation, preservation and gathering. Civic AI and local computing projects offer potential tools and services.

The plan names these families without a direct public link. A practical connection still needs a specific contribution and agreement.

Ownership stays
with the agreement.

Independent makers, businesses, cooperatives, joint projects and mutuals can participate. A mutual is one option for shared purchasing or productive assets, chosen by its members.

Membership and decision arrangements belong to that enterprise. They do not become rules for everyone using the engine.

From the original plan, chapters 8, 9, 12 and 14. Read the source PDF.
